WHy ſhould I haſten hither, ſince the good I bring to men is ſlowly underſtood? If then, the need of what is good, Doth make it lov'd, or underſtood, Or tis by abſence better knowne I ſhall be valew'd, when I'm gonne. Should dewes not fall, the Sunne forbeare His courſe, or I my viſits here; Alike from theſe defects would ceaſe The power and hope, of all increaſe. I will! and much I grieve, that though the beſt Of Kingly ſcience, harbours in his breſt, Yet tis his fate, to rule in adverſe times, When wiſedome muſt awhile give place to crimes.
I know it is the Peoples vice, To lay too meane, too cheape a price On ev'ry bleſsing they poſſeſſe Th'injoying makes them thinke it leſſe. Yet ſtay! O ſtay! if but to pleaſe The great and wiſe Philogenes. Stay then! O ſtay! If but to eaſe The cares of wiſe Philogenes.
O who but he, could thus endure To live, and governe in a ſulleine age, When it is harder far to cure, The Peoples folly than reſiſt their rage?
